title: Davenant: refuge-embrace always justifies; vivid sense of pardon is faith's daughter
source_text: CXVII. Probavimus quoque idem cum Amesio sentire hac in parte Davenantium. Nam juxta ipsum, fiduciae vocabulum duo designat. Primo, ipsum actum innitendi & adhaerendi Jesu Christo, quo quasi ambabus ulnis Christum amplectimur, & per eum actum veniam, gratiam & gloriam conamur obtinere a Deo Patre: atque hunc putat esse illum actum, quem semper sequitur justificatio, id est, absolutio a peccatis, & acceptatio in gratiam favoremque divinum; sive peccator illo ipso primo momento animo concipiat obtentae remissionis, sive non. Secundo, solet etiam aliquando fiducia denotare consequens effectum fidei justificantis, nempe plenam persuasionem, & quasi vividum sensum remissionis impetratae, & obtenti favoris divini. Et fatetur hanc fiduciam non esse fidem justificantem, sed fidei justificantis filiam, quam anima justificata, nonnisi post multa fidei & sanctitatis exercitia solet eniti.
pass_a_gloss: We have also proved that Davenant feels the same with Ames on this point. For according to him, the word trust designates two things. First, the very act of leaning on and adhering to Jesus Christ, by which as with both arms we embrace Christ, and through that act we endeavor to obtain pardon, grace, and glory from God the Father: and this he judges to be that act which justification always follows — that is, absolution from sins, and acceptance into divine grace and favor — whether or not the sinner at that very first moment conceives in his mind the remission obtained. Second, trust is also sometimes wont to denote the consequent effect of justifying faith, namely full persuasion, and as it were a vivid sense of pardon obtained, and of divine favor gained. And he confesses that this trust is not justifying faith, but the daughter of justifying faith, which the justified soul is wont to bring forth only after many exercises of faith and holiness.
pass_b_english: Davenant agrees with Ames: 'trust' names two things.
First — embracing Christ with both arms to obtain pardon, grace, and glory — always followed by justification, whether or not the sinner instantly feels remission gained.
Second — vivid persuasion of pardon already obtained — is justifying faith's daughter, born only after much exercise of faith and holiness.

lemmas.gloss: the act of leaning on and adhering to Jesus Christ
a vivid sense of remission obtained

rejected: assurance as the justifying act itself
